Stoat

DownloadLive previewDocsSupport

Stoat is a tiny WordPress theme — around a 103 KB zip, almost no JavaScript, and no Google Fonts.

Overview

Stoat is a minimal, fast-loading WordPress theme built for blogs and personal sites. The whole theme zip is about 103 KB and ships roughly 15 KB of compressed CSS in a single stylesheet, uses almost no JavaScript, and loads no Google Fonts — so pages stay light and quick on every device. A clean Stoat site scores around 99/100 on Lighthouse mobile out of the box, with no caching plugin, CDN, or tracking code required.

There’s no page builder to get between you and your writing. Fonts are self-hosted through WordPress’s Font Library (WordPress 7.0+), with a system-font fallback on older versions, and the editor is styled to match the front end so what you write is what you get.

Features

  • Latest version 1.3 (updated July 17, 2026)
  • Tiny ~103 KB theme zip
  • WordPress 7.0 ready, PHP 7 & 8 ready
  • Tiny JS, no page builder
  • ~15 KB of compressed CSS, one stylesheet
  • Self-hosted fonts via WordPress’s Font Library (WordPress 7.0+)
  • Responsive, looks great on all devices
  • Text or image logo
  • Two menu locations: primary and footer
  • Beautiful typography and editor
  • Layout: content width, narrow or full for archives, pages, and posts
  • Header: light or dark skin, custom colors, and an optional call-to-action button
  • Separate nav, heading and body fonts, with heading weight and letter case
  • Archive thumbnail ratio and width, plus styled Query Loop blocks
  • Wide-image and fullscreen image for writing
  • Translation-ready
  • Toggle to show or hide most things on the blog and single post

FAQs

Is this theme free?

Yes, you can use it for your website, for commercial and non-commercial purposes. However, you can't redistribute it or resell it in any form.

Do I need to keep credit to WiThemes?

No, you don't have to. But we're thankful if you do ^^

Can I use it on WordPress.com?

WordPress.com requires a paid plan before you can install a third-party theme or plugin. So yes, you can — but it requires a paid plan, starting from Personal ($4/month).

Will you maintain and update it?

Yes. We will maintain it. This is a long-term project.

Changelog

Version 1.3 — Jul 17, 2026

- new: content width and narrow reading column in pixels, plus narrow or full width for archives, pages, and posts (Customize > Layout)
- new: per-page content width override in the page editor's "Page options" box
- new: light or dark header skin, header background and text colors, and header padding (Customize > Header)
- new: header button with primary/black/white/outline styles and an optional new tab; moves into the off-canvas menu on mobile (Customize > Header)
- new: show the featured image above the post content, with its caption (Customize > Single Post)
- new: footer padding (Customize > Footer)
- the footer now follows the content width above it instead of always using the reading column
- styled the Button block in the editor to match the front end, and styled the Details block

Version 1.2.2 — Jul 16, 2026

- new: navigation font, heading font weight, and heading letter case (Customize > Typography)
- new: meta text color for the date, categories, and comment count (Customize > Style)
- new: thumbnail ratio and thumbnail width for the archive (Customize > Blog / Archive)
- styled the core Query Loop blocks so they match the theme's own archive
- fixed: a 404 URL rendered the full post archive under the "Nothing found" heading
- fixed: two roles sharing one font family emitted that family's @font-face rules twice
- heading spacing and list indentation now apply everywhere, not only inside post content

Version 1.2.1 — Jun 23, 2026

- updated screenshot.jpg and documented the CC0 license/credits for the images used in it

Version 1.2 — Jun 19, 2026

- minor style refinements

Version 1.1.1 — Jun 09, 2026

- mobile menu open/close is now pure CSS + inline handlers; Esc and focus-trap moved to an optional js/a11y.js (Customize > Misc)
- removed the classic-editor toggle (use the official Classic Editor plugin instead)
- "disable pages in search results" now defaults off

Version 1.1 — Jun 08, 2026

- fix bugs when tested carefully

Version 1.0 — Jun 07, 2026

- initial release

Updates & support

Stoat is actively maintained — it powers the author’s personal site, miketran.net. Updates ship through the official WordPress.org theme directory, so you’ll be notified inside your dashboard whenever a new version is available.

Need help? Start with the documentation, or post in the WordPress.org support forum.
